purpose: Architectural closeout of C5 with the identity-strength boundary finding. This artifact records lifecycle governance and architecture findings only: it does not reopen or rerun any C5 evaluation, does not modify any resolver code, and makes no retrieval-performance or fusion claim.

status_distinction.note: C5-A1 PASS means the resolver implementation satisfied its preregistered architecture/safety contract; it does NOT mean every unique exact match is semantically sufficient canonical identity. C5-A3 PASS means this architectural/governance closeout was completed correctly. The C5 evaluation verdict remains INCONCLUSIVE and the lifecycle becomes CLOSED_INCONCLUSIVE, which is intentionally neither C5 = PASS nor C5 = FAIL.

blocker_a_descriptive_resolution_evidenc.statement: The central intended capability (descriptive human terminology -> canonical technical entity -> better exact retrieval) could not be evaluated because no accepted alias occurs whole in the locked English pool. Creating aliases now from the exposed Gold pool would be benchmark fitting and is not authorized.

blocker_b_identity_strength_underspecifi.statement: A unique exact database match is not sufficient evidence that an object deserves unconditional canonical-prefix promotion.

representative_observed_mechanism.outcome: relevant evidence was displaced; MRR decreased

blocker_b_identity_strength_underspecifi.interpretation: This is not evidence that the string match was incorrect. It is evidence that unique retrieval match != strong canonical entity identity != automatic retrieval-priority entitlement.

canonicality_review_finding.authoritative_finding: Exact-match uniqueness alone is insufficient evidence of canonical entity identity for all object types.
canonicality_review_finding.semantics: These may identify a relevant database object without proving that the object itself is the canonical entity representation intended by the user mention.
canonicality_review_finding.a1_status_recorded_as: C5-A1 = PASS under its original preregistered contract
canonicality_review_finding.post_evaluation_architecture_finding: the original canonicality contract was too permissive for weak identity evidence

identity_strength_boundary.scope: governance/design documentation only; NOT implemented in production code by C5-A3
strong_identity_evidence_examples: exact locator.symbol when the object representation genuinely carries symbol identity
explicit stable canonical entity identifier if/when such schema exists
future identity/equivalence relation only when relation semantics unambiguously mean identity
weak_retrieval_match_examples: documentation object sharing the queried name
identity_strength_boundary.rule: Weak matches may be useful retrieval candidates. They must NOT automatically imply canonical identity or unconditional rank-1 prefix promotion.

canonical_locator_finding.statement: The C5-A0 inventory identified canonical_locator as an available exact field, but the current resolver's exact lookup primarily uses locator.symbol, title, locator.path, and path basename, and does not establish a dedicated canonical-identity semantic contract for canonical_locator.
canonical_locator_finding.future_design_input: Do NOT assume that the existence of the canonical_locator field implies every canonical_locator value is an entity identity key; its semantics must be inspected generically before future use.

historical_evidence_summary.mrr_interpretation_rule: The MRR regression must be reinterpreted neither as 'entity resolution was generally incorrect' nor as merely 'a fusion issue'. The correct interpretation: the existing canonical-prefix eligibility semantics are too broad for weak identity matches.

reasons: 2 the diagnostic exact cohort produced no improvement and three regressions
3 the identity-strength/canonical-prefix contract requires future refinement
4 production benefit has not been established

reactivation_dependency.primary_dependency: Phase D / new generic entity infrastructure

valid_triggers: systematic accepted aliases from Phase D
generic identity-strength policy designed independently of the exposed C5 cohort
new independently-authored evaluation data suitable for descriptive entity resolution
invalid_triggers: more existing Gold cases are available
someone wants to tune the PandaRoot case
reopen_rule.form: C5 may be reopened only as a new explicitly authorized architectural task with genuinely new information/capability.

c6_dependency_correction.reason: C6 can evaluate the currently valid production channels: exact = LEGACY_EXACT, raw_dense = production-authoritative, semantic_dense = auxiliary/shadow, sparse = raw question, paper, workflow, graph. C6 does NOT require EntityFirstExact to be production-authoritative.
c6_ownership_unchanged: future evaluation of whether entity-aware information should influence sparse or exact fusion behavior

downstream_ownership.c4: evaluation verdict INCONCLUSIVE, lifecycle CLOSED_INCONCLUSIVE, production sparse raw question; C4 not reopened; no C5 finding fed into LexicalQueryBuilder
downstream_ownership.phase_d: NOT_STARTED; owns richer entity schema, systematic alias migration, canonical entity representation, broader resolver semantics, identity relations, incremental shortcut migration
downstream_ownership.phase_e: NOT_STARTED; g011 remains deferred to Phase E; g011 must not justify C5 resolver changes; answer-point coverage / missing-evidence logic stays out of C5
